subject: OpenBank discovery — token economics recap & budget constraints
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-18T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: OpenBank discovery — token economics recap & budget constraints

Alex / Priya — great conversation earlier, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed set of next steps so we keep momentum. This is a short summary focused on cost/TCO levers we discussed.

Pain points you called out
- Real-time fraud chat summaries for fraud ops are spiking costs (current system estimates ~3.2M tokens/month at peak; token distribution skewed by 25% of sessions).
- Latency sensitivity on first-touch pipelines (SLO: 300ms P95) — batching helps but can't harm live UX.
- Procurement/budget window for Q2 is tight: you have ~$80k incremental budget for pilots.

Goals you shared
- Reduce per-interaction inference cost by >=40% while preserving model fidelity for high-risk flows.
- Validate a production pattern that meets 300ms P95 in our EU/US regions.
- Run a 6–8 week pilot with clearly measured ROI and a go/no-go gate for a broader rollout.

Token economics & levers we recommend (back-of-envelope from call)
- Current baseline: ~0.8 tokens/sec average per session, 3.2M tokens/mo.
- Batching: grouping 4–6 concurrent short chats yields ~25–35% cost savings for non-real-time paths.
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated customer-context reduces tokens by 18–22% on summary flows.
- Quantization-profile: INT8 for background scoring, FP16 for fraud-detection paths — expected extra latency <20ms, cost cut ~30% on scoring workloads.

Pilot scope suggestion (attached pilot_scope.xlsx)
- 2 endpoints: (1) fraud-summary offline/batched path; (2) first-touch live path with strict latency SLO.
- Duration: 6 weeks (2 weeks instrumentation + 4 weeks live sampling at 25% traffic).
- Success metrics: unit cost per session, P95 latency, % of degraded responses needing manual review, and projected monthly cost at 100% traffic.

Estimated budget ask
- Estimated Redwood incremental spend for pilot: $45k–$60k (depending on capacity selection and burst needs).
- Redwood recommends starting on Dedicated reserve for predictable throughput for the live path; hosted for batched offline path.

Next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm procurement window (is Q2 budget commit firm)?
2) Please share the procurement contact or SOW owner (we need contact for PO terms).
3) Confirm a target start week (we penciled Mar 8 in the attached plan).

Attachments: openbank_discovery_notes.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB) and pilot_scope.xlsx (Excel, 240KB).

Thanks — will drop a short one-pager if you'd like a compact version for your finance team.

— Soojin

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well with our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget: the $80k is confirmed as an incremental pilot pot for Q2 but needs an internal sign-off from finance (Daniel will need the one-pager you mentioned). If we can keep Redwood line-item under $60k we have a strong chance of green-lighting without exec escalation.
2) Latency: for the live first-touch path we cannot exceed 300ms P95 — anything above will require us to funnel to a lighter fallback model (which you suggested).
3) Data residency: logs for EU customers must remain in EU region — can you confirm Redwood Dedicated can pin region and retain logs per our compliance needs?

Also copying Daniel Ortiz, our procurement lead, to route SOW and PO questions.

Alex

Head of Payments Product, OpenBank

Alex — thanks for the quick note and the clarifications. Short answers below and next actions so Daniel has what he needs.

Answers:
- Budget: we can target the pilot at the $45k–$60k range. I’ll prepare the one-pager with a clear breakdown (engineering hours, reserved capacity, expected token spend).
- Latency: yes — Dedicated can pin to US/EU regions and we can configure routing so EU traffic stays in EU. For P95 <300ms we recommend the live path use a small Dedicated pool with warm KV cache; fallback to a smaller quantized model if SLO is violated.
- Data residency & logs: Redwood Private/Dedicated supports region pinning and log retention controls. We’ll include the compliance note in the SOW.

Immediate next actions (I’ll take lead)
- I’ll send a 1-page budget breakdown and an abbreviated SOW draft to Daniel by EOD tomorrow (2027-02-19).
- Vivek, can you prepare a short tech appendix describing the quantization and caching configuration we propose for OpenBank? (cc’d).
- Alex / Priya: confirm if Mar 8 works to start instrumentation; if not suggest alternatives.

Attachment: updated pilot_scope.xlsx (I added a budget line-item and timetable).

— Soojin
